title: 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Thessalonians chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5.

questions.question: In 1 Thessalonians 5, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: But of the times and the seasons
For when they shall say, Peace and safety
But ye, brethren, are not in darkness
questions.correctAnswer: But of the times and the seasons
questions.explanation: This phrase appears first in the chapter, specifically in 1 Thessalonians 5:1.

questions.question: What does 1 Thessalonians 5:2 say about the day of the Lord?
options: It comes as a thief in the night
It will be announced with a trumpet
It occurs after a great battle
questions.correctAnswer: It comes as a thief in the night
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:2 states that the day of the Lord cometh as a thief in the night.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in 1 Thessalonians 5:3 when they say, 'Peace and safety'?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:3 states that when they say 'Peace and safety', then sudden destruction cometh upon them.

questions.question: According to 1 Thessalonians 5:4, what are the brethren not in?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:4 states that the brethren are not in darkness.

questions.question: What are believers referred to in 1 Thessalonians 5:5?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:5 describes believers as all the children of light.

questions.question: What does 1 Thessalonians 5:6 urge believers to do?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:6 urges believers to not sleep, but to watch and be sober.

questions.question: In 1 Thessalonians 5:7, who is said to sleep?
options: They that sleep in the night
questions.correctAnswer: They that sleep in the night
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:7 mentions that they that sleep sleep in the night.

questions.question: What should those of the day put on according to 1 Thessalonians 5:8?
options: The breastplate of faith and love
questions.correctAnswer: The breastplate of faith and love
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:8 states that those who are of the day should put on the breastplate of faith and love.

questions.question: What has God not appointed us to, according to 1 Thessalonians 5:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:9 states that God hath not appointed us to wrath.

questions.question: Who died for us, according to 1 Thessalonians 5:10?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:10 states that Jesus Christ died for us.

questions.question: In 1 Thessalonians 5:10, what should we do whether we wake or sleep?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:10 states that whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him.

questions.question: Is it true that the day of the Lord comes unexpectedly?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:2 indicates that the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night, suggesting it is unexpected.

questions.question: Is it true that believers are described as children of the night?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:5 clarifies that believers are children of light, not children of the night.

questions.question: Is it false that believers are urged to sleep according to 1 Thessalonians 5:6?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:6 urges believers to not sleep, which makes the statement false.

questions.question: Is it false that God has appointed us to destruction according to 1 Thessalonians 5:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:9 states that God hath not appointed us to wrath, which makes this statement false.

medium.title: 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What are believers encouraged to do in 1 Thessalonians 5:11?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:11 states, 'Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.'

questions.question: What does 1 Thessalonians 5:12 promise will happen if you know those who labor among you?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Thessalonians 5:13 encourages believers to 'be at peace among yourselves' as a result of knowing those who labor among them.

questions.question: How are believers instructed to treat those who are unruly according to 1 Thessalonians 5:14?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Thessalonians 5:14 states, 'Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly...'

questions.question: What does 1 Thessalonians 5:15 advise against doing?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:15 warns, 'See that none render evil for evil unto any man...'

questions.question: What should believers do continuously according to 1 Thessalonians 5:17?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Thessalonians 5:17 explicitly states, 'Pray without ceasing.'

questions.question: What is the will of God concerning believers as stated in 1 Thessalonians 5:18?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:18 says, 'In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.'

questions.question: According to 1 Thessalonians 5:19, what should believers not do?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:19 states, 'Quench not the Spirit.'

questions.question: What should believers do with prophesyings, as stated in 1 Thessalonians 5:20?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Thessalonians 5:20 warns, 'Despise not prophesyings.'

questions.question: What is a key attitude believers should have towards their leaders as per 1 Thessalonians 5:13?
options: Esteem them very highly in love
questions.correctAnswer: Esteem them very highly in love
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:13 instructs believers to 'esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake.'

questions.question: How should believers support the weak according to 1 Thessalonians 5:14?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 1 Thessalonians 5:14 advises believers to 'be patient toward all men' when supporting the weak.

questions.question: What does 1 Thessalonians 5:16 emphasize about joy?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:16 states, 'Rejoice evermore.'

questions.question: According to 1 Thessalonians 5:3, what will happen when they say 'Peace and safety'?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:3 warns that 'then sudden destruction cometh upon them...'.

questions.question: Is it true that believers are called the children of light according to 1 Thessalonians 5:5?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:5 states, 'Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day...'.

questions.question: Is it true that 1 Thessalonians 5:2 states the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the day?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:2 mentions that the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night, not in the day.

questions.question: Is it true that 1 Thessalonians 5:9 says God has appointed us to wrath?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 1 Thessalonians 5:9 clearly states that God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation.

hard.title: 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5.

questions.question: What are we instructed to do with all things according to 1 Thessalonians 5:21?
questions.explanation: This is stated in 1 Thessalonians 5:21, where it says 'Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.'

questions.question: Which of the following is a directive found in 1 Thessalonians 5:22?
options: Abstain from all appearance of evil
questions.correctAnswer: Abstain from all appearance of evil
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:22 explicitly instructs, 'Abstain from all appearance of evil.'

questions.question: What does Paul pray for in 1 Thessalonians 5:23?
options: That they may be sanctified wholly
questions.correctAnswer: That they may be sanctified wholly
questions.explanation: In 1 Thessalonians 5:23, Paul prays, 'And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly.'

questions.question: According to 1 Thessalonians 5:24, who is faithful to call us?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:24 states, 'Faithful is he that calleth you,' referring to God.

questions.question: What does Paul ask the brethren to do in 1 Thessalonians 5:25?
questions.explanation: In 1 Thessalonians 5:25, Paul says, 'Brethren, pray for us.'

questions.question: What does Paul charge in 1 Thessalonians 5:27?
options: To read this epistle to all holy brethren
questions.correctAnswer: To read this epistle to all holy brethren
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:27 states, 'I charge you by the Lord that this epistle be read unto all the holy brethren.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'proven' in 1 Thessalonians 5:21 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'prove' (dokimazo) means to test or examine.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 uses parallelism with the repeated structure of commands: rejoice, pray, give thanks.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of being children of light in 1 Thessalonians 5:5?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:8 states, 'For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light.' This echoes the theme of 1 Thessalonians 5:5.

questions.question: Which passage fulfills the directive to pray without ceasing found in 1 Thessalonians 5:17?
questions.explanation: Luke 18:1 emphasizes the importance of persistent prayer, aligning with the command in 1 Thessalonians 5:17.

questions.question: What comes immediately before 1 Thessalonians 5:21?
options: Abstain from all appearance of evil
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:20, which states 'Despise not prophesyings,' comes immediately before 5:21.

questions.question: The Greek word 'hagios' in 1 Thessalonians 5:27 means what?
questions.explanation: 'Hagios' means 'holy' and is used in 1 Thessalonians 5:27 in reference to the brethren.

questions.question: What literary device is present in 1 Thessalonians 5:14 regarding the actions towards others?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:14 uses climax in the series of actions: warn, comfort, support, reflecting increasing intensity.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Thessalonians 5:18 instructs to give thanks in every situation.
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:18 states, 'In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.'

questions.question: True or False: 1 Thessalonians 5:25 encourages the brethren to pray for themselves only.
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:25 specifically says, 'Brethren, pray for us,' indicating they should pray for Paul and his companions.

theological.title: 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Thessalonians Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Thessalonians 5:9 teach about salvation?
options: God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ
Salvation is earned by works and human effort
God predestines some to wrath and others to salvation arbitrarily
Salvation is uncertain and depends on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:9 clearly states that God has not appointed believers to wrath but to obtain salvation through Jesus Christ, affirming the doctrine of salvation by grace through Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Thessalonians 5:23 teach about sanctification?
options: God sanctifies believers wholly, preserving spirit, soul, and body blameless unto Christ's coming
Sanctification is a human effort independent of God's work
Only the soul is sanctified, while body remains sinful
Sanctification is partial and never complete in this life
questions.correctAnswer: God sanctifies believers wholly, preserving spirit, soul, and body blameless unto Christ's coming
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:23 teaches that God, as the God of peace, sanctifies the whole person—spirit, soul, and body—and preserves them blameless until the coming of Jesus Christ, emphasizing divine sanctification in entirety.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian conduct does 1 Thessalonians 5:15 teach?
options: Believers must never render evil for evil but always pursue that which is good toward all
It is permissible to repay evil with evil for justice
Christian conduct is indifferent toward how one treats others
Good conduct is only required toward fellow believers, not all men
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must never render evil for evil but always pursue that which is good toward all
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:15 instructs believers to avoid repaying evil with evil and to always follow good toward everyone, underscoring the doctrine of holy and loving Christian ethics.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Thessalonians 5:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:24 says 'Faithful is he that calleth you,' highlighting God's attribute of faithfulness in calling and completing the salvation of believers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in 1 Thessalonians 5:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:9 emphasizes that God has not appointed believers to wrath but to obtain salvation through Jesus Christ, demonstrating His attribute of mercy.

questions.question: How does 1 Thessalonians 5:1-2 prepare for New Testament eschatology?
options: It teaches the unexpected and sudden nature of the Day of the Lord akin to a thief in the night
It predicts exact dates for Christ’s return
It denies any future Day of the Lord
It teaches that the Day of the Lord will be announced by visible signs
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the unexpected and sudden nature of the Day of the Lord akin to a thief in the night
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 describe the Day of the Lord coming unexpectedly, like a thief in the night, preparing readers for the New Testament eschatological teaching on the suddenness of Christ’s return.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 1 Thessalonians 5:10 have with Christ's atonement?
options: Christ died so that believers, whether awake or asleep, might live together with Him
Christ's death only benefits those who are awake and active in works
His death does not guarantee resurrection
Christ’s death is symbolic and not efficacious for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Christ died so that believers, whether awake or asleep, might live together with Him
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:10 teaches that Christ’s death secures eternal life for believers regardless of their state (awake or asleep), linking His atoning work to resurrection and eternal fellowship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 5 and 8 teach about Christian identity and protection?
options: Believers are children of light and of the day, who protect themselves by faith, love, and hope
Believers live in darkness and must rely on works alone
Christian identity is irrelevant to spiritual protection
Only ritual observance protects believers from evil
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are children of light and of the day, who protect themselves by faith, love, and hope
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 8 together reveal believers as children of light and day who must be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love and the helmet of hope, symbolizing spiritual protection and identity.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about the Spirit and prophecy is found in verses 19 and 20?
options: Believers must not quench the Spirit nor despise prophecies, affirming openness to Spirit-led revelation
The Spirit is to be rejected and prophecy disregarded
Quenching the Spirit is encouraged to maintain order
Prophecy is to be accepted without any testing
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must not quench the Spirit nor despise prophecies, affirming openness to Spirit-led revelation
questions.explanation: Verses 19 and 20 instruct believers not to quench the Spirit or despise prophecies, emphasizing the doctrine of ongoing Spirit-empowered revelation in the church.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about discernment and holiness is taught in verses 21 and 22?
options: Believers must prove all things, hold fast to the good, and abstain from all appearance of evil
All things are to be accepted without testing
Appearance of evil is permissible if intentions are good
Discernment is unnecessary in Christian life
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must prove all things, hold fast to the good, and abstain from all appearance of evil
questions.explanation: Verses 21 and 22 teach the necessity of testing all things, keeping what is good, and avoiding the appearance of evil, emphasizing both discernment and holiness.

questions.question: What doctrine emerges when synthesizing 1 Thessalonians 5:6 and 5:16-18 about Christian vigilance and spiritual discipline?
options: Believers must watch and be sober, rejoicing always, praying without ceasing, and giving thanks in all things
Sleepiness and spiritual lethargy are acceptable
Prayer and rejoicing are optional spiritual activities
Vigilance is only necessary during persecution
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must watch and be sober, rejoicing always, praying without ceasing, and giving thanks in all things
questions.explanation: Verse 6 calls for sobriety and watchfulness, while verses 16-18 urge constant rejoicing, unceasing prayer, and thanksgiving, together forming a comprehensive doctrine of spiritual vigilance and discipline.

questions.question: Skeptics claim 1 Thessalonians 5:19-21 teaches that prophecy is unquestionable and must be accepted without testing. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Believers must not quench the Spirit nor despise prophecies but must prove all things and hold fast to what is good
Prophecy is infallible and requires no discernment
Only apostles can prophesy and no testing is needed
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must not quench the Spirit nor despise prophecies but must prove all things and hold fast to what is good
questions.explanation: Verses 19-21 command openness to the Spirit and prophecy but also instruct believers to test all things and hold onto what is good, refuting the claim that prophecy is beyond scrutiny.

questions.question: What doctrine about pastoral authority does 1 Thessalonians 5:12-13 teach?
options: Believers are to know and esteem those who labor and have oversight in the Lord, honoring them for their work
Leaders must be feared rather than loved
Only apostles have authority in the church
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are to know and esteem those who labor and have oversight in the Lord, honoring them for their work
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 exhort believers to recognize and highly esteem church leaders who labor among them, teaching the doctrine of pastoral authority and respect.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 1 Thessalonians 5:28's benediction?
questions.explanation: The closing verse 5:28 pronounces 'The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you,' emphasizing God's gracious nature toward believers.

questions.question: What theological synthesis is seen in 1 Thessalonians 5:4 and 5 regarding believers' state in relation to the Day of the Lord?
options: Believers are not in darkness and thus will not be overtaken like a thief; they are children of light and day
Believers will be overtaken unawares like the rest
All are equally in darkness and night
Believers dwell in spiritual night and must be saved from it
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are not in darkness and thus will not be overtaken like a thief; they are children of light and day
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 state that believers are not in darkness and are called children of light and day, indicating their spiritual vigilance and assurance against surprise at the Day of the Lord.
